values.description: Materialize only selected repository paths, including cone-mode patterns and later selective expansion, to reduce client working-tree scope.

values.label: Compressed Git index
values.description: Index compression reduces client-side repository metadata size.

values.label: Built-in filesystem monitor
values.description: Git's filesystem monitor accelerates status and add operations in repositories with many working-tree files.

values.label: Rails monolith
values.description: The application begins and largely remains a Rails monolith around repository access.

values.label: On-demand object retrieval
values.description: Fetch repository objects dynamically when clients need them instead of transferring the complete object history initially.

values.label: Single-file index management
values.description: Represent and process the complete tracked-path index as one file for core working-directory commands.

values.label: Interrupted clone progress loss
values.description: Immediate server reboot can discard progress from a long-running clone that must restart elsewhere.

values.label: Reduced initial clone footprint
values.description: Filtered object transfer substantially reduces the client download compared with transferring complete repository history.

values.label: Reduced index storage footprint
values.description: An updated index representation lowers storage and I/O burden for repositories with millions of tracked paths.

values.label: Low per-entry index processing cost
values.description: Single-file index processing can retain low average cost per tracked entry despite a very large repository.

values.label: Git untracked cache
values.description: Cache information about untracked paths to reduce repeated working-directory inspection for repositories with many files.

values.label: Default sparse clone initialization
values.description: Client clones initially populate only a minimal directory set, with user-controlled expansion or a full-clone override.

values.label: Populated-file modification detection cost
values.description: Detecting modifications among populated working-directory files imposes additional client-side processing cost.

values.label: Compatibility-limited advanced-feature defaults
values.description: Advanced performance features remain disabled by default when enabling them broadly could reduce compatibility.

values.label: GVFS protocol integration
values.description: Scalar supports the ecosystem-specific GVFS protocol alongside standard Git performance mechanisms.

values.label: GVFS protocol standardization
values.description: The GVFS protocol is made a standard feature of the core Git client.

values.label: Linux support
values.description: The specialized client provides supported Linux operation.

values.label: Git-aware custom filesystem watcher
values.description: Uses a Git-specific watcher that respects repository exclusions instead of a general-purpose filesystem watcher.

values.label: Watchman-based filesystem watching
values.description: Uses the general-purpose Watchman tool to detect working-tree changes.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem working-tree scaling
values.description: Uses a virtualized filesystem to defer populated working-tree costs and accelerate checkout presentation.

values.label: Local Git configuration setup
values.description: Initializes repository-local performance settings as part of enabling the scaling client experience.

values.label: Hourly background fetch
values.description: Remote objects are fetched periodically outside foreground commands while ordinary local and remote-tracking branches remain unchanged.

values.label: Background commit-graph maintenance
values.description: Commit graphs and multi-pack indexes are updated asynchronously to keep large-history operations efficient.

values.label: Incremental reachable-commit graph
values.description: Split incremental commit-graph files include reachable commits while limiting repeated update cost.

values.label: User-suspendable background maintenance
values.description: Automated repository maintenance can be paused or stopped by the user.

values.label: Incremental bounded pack repacking
values.description: Small pack batches are rewritten incrementally to control client repository maintenance cost.

values.label: Multi-pack-index pack migration
values.description: A multi-pack index redirects objects to replacement packs before obsolete packs expire.

values.label: Two-phase repack and expire
values.description: Pack rewriting and obsolete-pack deletion run as separate maintenance operations.

values.label: Background Git object-database maintenance
values.description: Expensive object-database cleanup runs in the background instead of blocking routine commands.

values.label: Ahead/behind calculation suppression
values.description: Interactive status omits expensive ahead/behind comparison.

values.label: Pack-file handle pressure
values.description: Unbounded pack counts create file-handle pressure during Git operations.

values.label: Improved delta-encoding efficiency
values.description: Pack rewriting can improve delta encoding and reduce repository storage.

values.label: Small-pack batch selection
values.description: Each incremental repack selects a bounded set of small packfiles.

values.label: Deferred obsolete-pack deletion
values.description: Old packs are deleted only after index references are safely migrated.

values.label: GVFS deployment without cache infrastructure
values.description: Whether GVFS is deployed without the cache-server infrastructure required for sufficiently large repositories.

values.label: Git-protocol Scalar registration
values.description: Using ordinary Git protocol access with Scalar registration when GVFS infrastructure is unavailable.

values.label: Insufficient scale for GVFS
values.description: Repository and user scale too small to justify GVFS protocol and cache infrastructure.

values.label: Watchman filesystem monitoring
values.description: Using Watchman with Git fsmonitor to detect working-tree changes efficiently.

values.label: Selective modified-path inspection
values.description: Restricting index and cache work to paths reported as changed instead of scanning every populated path.

values.label: Git status latency reduction
values.description: Lowering status latency by avoiding full working-directory inspection in very large repositories.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem working-tree scaling
values.description: Using a virtualized filesystem to scale large-repository working trees by avoiding ordinary Git size assumptions.

values.label: Non-virtualized large-repository support
values.description: Scaling very large repositories with Git and client optimizations without requiring a virtualized filesystem.

values.label: Trace-driven bottleneck identification
values.description: Using tracing and user feedback to identify repository performance bottlenecks for targeted improvements.

values.label: Single-pack full repacking
values.description: Rewriting all repository objects into one consolidated pack-file during maintenance.

values.label: Per-pack index scanning overhead
values.description: Lookup degradation caused by scanning an increasingly large collection of pack indexes.

values.label: Single-pack-equivalent object lookup
values.description: Preserving object lookup performance comparable to a repository consolidated into one pack-file.

iterations.explanation: Moved persistence and replication values from 9 to 10, consistency to 6, routing to 11; renamed 6 and 10 for clearer axes.

clusters.name: Repository Storage Representation
clusters.description: Which repository hosting substrate, access form, and Git storage representation is used?

relations.reading: Choices on Repository Storage Representation affect the outcomes of Write Commitment and Consistency
relations.rationale: Replica count and placement determine whether quorum or synchronous durability requirements can be met and influence capacity and latency.

values.label: Centralized repository hosting
values.description: A centralized service provides the primary repository access point despite Git's distributed capabilities.

values.label: Single-machine repository storage
values.description: Application software and repository copies initially coexist on one powerful machine.

values.label: Filesystem-level repository distribution
values.description: Repositories are distributed through the filesystem layer to scale application instances without changing Rails or Git internals.

values.label: NFS-based centralized repository storage
values.description: NFS is considered for centralized storage but rejected because Git's local-filesystem assumptions do not work safely or efficiently over it.

values.label: Networked-filesystem repository access
values.description: The attempted networked-filesystem approach produces poor performance and buggy behavior because of mismatched filesystem assumptions.

values.label: DHT-backed Git object storage
values.description: Stores individual Git objects in a distributed hash table instead of repository packfiles.

values.label: Object-level repository distribution
values.description: Distributes individual content-addressed objects across storage nodes rather than preserving repository-level packfile organization.

values.label: JGit repository-storage abstraction
values.description: Uses replaceable JGit storage interfaces to change repository storage while retaining Git operations.

values.label: Packfile-based repository storage
values.description: Stores repository code and metadata in compressed Git packfiles.

values.label: Dedicated fileserver repository hosting
values.description: Keeps repositories on dedicated fileservers and exposes repository operations through remote procedure calls.

values.label: Whole-file local repository caching
values.description: Caches a complete repository file locally to accelerate random access to repository data.

values.label: Delta-compressed packfile storage
values.description: Stores most packfile objects as deltas to reduce storage size at the cost of additional read hops.

values.label: Packfile-based Git networking
values.description: Uses Git packfiles as the client-server transfer representation regardless of internal server storage.

values.label: Packfile size-minimizing layout
values.description: Places Git objects in packfiles using a compact size-minimization heuristic rather than preserving repository-DAG locality.

values.label: Git-level distribution
values.description: Repository distribution modifies or distributes Git itself rather than replicating repository data above it.

values.label: Repository-data transformation
values.description: Repository contents are transformed into a separate client-facing storage format.

values.label: Application layer over unmodified Git
values.description: Hosting features are built above standard Git repositories without maintaining a Git fork.

values.label: Plain Git repositories on local NVMe
values.description: Native repositories are stored on local NVMe for random-read performance and client compatibility.

clusters.name: Replica Topology and Persistence
clusters.description: Which replica placement and durable state model maintains repository copies across failures?

relations.reading: Choices on Replica Topology and Persistence affect the outcomes of Write Commitment and Consistency
relations.rationale: S3-backed authoritative state, freshness validation, and elastic replica topology change consistency and write-commitment behavior.

values.label: Cross-rack replica placement
values.description: Replicas are distributed across racks to survive rack-level failures as well as individual node failures.

values.label: Three-replica repository topology
values.description: Each repository receives at least three copies to provide redundancy and capacity for continued operation after one machine failure.

values.label: Single-extra-copy topology
values.description: Keeping only one additional copy is considered sufficient for a single-node failure but rejected because concurrent writes still require consistent serialization.

values.label: Idle-replica overhead
values.description: Maintaining three mostly idle replicas per small or throwaway repository creates substantial overhead as repository counts proliferate.

values.label: Monorepo traffic capacity shortfall
values.description: Three replicas become insufficient for traffic from massive enterprise monorepos, especially continuous-integration traffic.

values.label: Write-ahead-log repository persistence
values.description: Authoritative repository state and provenance persist in a durable write-ahead log rather than fixed host placement.

values.label: Relational reference database persistence
values.description: Store repository references in an external relational database alongside blob or packfile storage.

values.label: Incremental replica checksum state
values.description: Maintain logical repository-state checksums incrementally rather than recomputing them from all references.

values.label: Full checksum recomputation
values.description: Recompute repository logical-state checksums from every reference after updates.

values.label: Pet-repository operational burden
values.description: Continuously tracking repository locations, validity, failures, and repairs creates substantial operational cost at scale.

values.label: Stateless repository placement
values.description: Repository placement is resolved from current healthy hosts without maintaining an external per-repository routing table.

values.label: Git application-level replication
values.description: Repository replication operates on Git-aware updates rather than filesystem blocks.

values.label: Proxy-mediated repository replication
values.description: A proxy transparently forwards each Git push to multiple repository replicas.

values.label: Low-latency replica placement
values.description: Replicas are placed near enough to coordinate updates within acceptable inter-replica communication latency.

values.label: Disk repository warm cache
values.description: Local disk repositories serve as reconstructible caches rather than fixed authoritative placement.

values.label: On-demand repository materialization
values.description: A host reconstructs an absent repository locally from durable log state when requests require it.

values.label: Rendezvous-hash placement hints
values.description: Repository identifiers rank expected healthy hosts without requiring authoritative placement state.

values.label: N-to-N replica reconstruction
values.description: Replacement replicas are created across the cluster from any surviving repository copies after failures.

values.label: ETag-validated replica freshness
values.description: Conditional object-store metadata validation confirms replica freshness before serving reads.

values.label: Read-time replica catch-up
values.description: Replicas apply newer durable log state before serving a read.

values.label: Elastic per-repository replica allocation
values.description: Replica count expands or contracts according to repository read demand and durable-source availability.

values.label: WAL-propagated compaction state
values.description: Compaction state is propagated through the authoritative log to keep replicas aligned.

values.label: Optimistic UDP catch-up gossip
values.description: Replicas exchange catch-up metadata through lossy gossip while durable reads independently validate freshness.

values.label: Compacted-data replica distribution
values.description: Replicas receive compacted repository data rather than maintaining unrelated storage states.

values.label: Arbitrary replica-based read scaling
values.description: Read replicas can be deployed in arbitrary numbers to scale read-only operations.

values.label: File-server content replication
values.description: Replicating repository and gist content stored on file servers across the application’s server fleet.

values.label: Repository repair and rebalancing
values.description: Repairing and redistributing repository copies as servers and networks fail or topology changes.

values.label: Durable highly available content access
values.description: Maintaining durable, highly available repository and gist access through copies distributed across failures.

values.label: Disk-backed repository source of truth
values.description: Repository data on local disks is treated as authoritative state rather than merely a reconstructible cache.

values.label: Filesystem block-level replication
values.description: Repository replicas are synchronized through filesystem block replication below Git's application semantics.

values.label: Co-located filesystem replica placement
values.description: Keeps filesystem replicas adjacent to control replication latency, rather than separating them across racks or sites.

values.label: S3 Express object-storage substrate
values.description: A low-latency object-storage tier is selected for high-throughput WAL persistence.

clusters.name: Write Commitment and Consistency
clusters.description: Which consistency, acknowledgment, locking, and refusal policy governs accepting repository writes?

relations.reading: Choices on Write Commitment and Consistency affect the outcomes of Repository Service Scaling
relations.rationale: Synchronous commitment, quorum locking, and refusal during insufficient replication can increase write latency or temporary request unavailability.

values.label: Three-phase commit consensus
values.description: Three-phase commit coordinates repository writes in a way that maps to the Git transaction model.

values.label: Consistency and partition tolerance priority
values.description: The system prioritizes consistency and partition tolerance over availability when those qualities conflict.

values.label: Synchronous write commitment
values.description: A write is accepted only after synchronous commitment establishes the durability promise.

values.label: Permanent data-loss resistance
values.description: Accepted pushes, merges, edits, and repository creations must not be corrupted or reverted.

values.label: Consensus tail-latency growth
values.description: Adding replicas increases the influence of the slowest participant on three-phase-commit latency.

values.label: Replica-count push-throughput degradation
values.description: Push throughput worsens as more replicas participate in three-phase commit.

values.label: Non-voting geo-replicated hosts
values.description: Geographically replicated hosts do not vote, allowing primary pushes to continue when a replicated host is unreachable.

values.label: WAL durability before push acknowledgement
values.description: Require durable operation-log persistence before reporting a successful push to the client.

values.label: Linearized repository operations
values.description: Process pushes and fundamental repository operations in one consistent order.

values.label: Operation-history replica rewind
values.description: Use recorded repository operations to rewind and fast-forward replicas without synchronizing through an external object or reference database.

values.label: Replica-based distributed locking
values.description: Replica coordination supplies distributed locks that order repository database updates.

values.label: Per-write ordering election
values.description: Each write directly elects its winning order and outcome instead of relying on a permanently elected primary.

values.label: Single-primary replication model
values.description: One elected primary copy determines authoritative write-arrival order for all replicas.

values.label: Replica coordination round-trip cost
values.description: Distributed replica coordination requires multiple network round trips, adding latency to repository operations.

values.label: Overlapped replica coordination work
values.description: Useful locking, checksum, and database work proceeds while replica network waits are outstanding.

values.label: Consensus-free arbitrary repository primaries
values.description: Any healthy server may accept a push without election because durable compare-and-swap synchronization makes concurrent updates safe.

values.label: Rendezvous-ranked primary preference
values.description: The highest-ranked healthy host is preferred to reduce compare-and-swap retries while other hosts remain valid.

values.label: Compare-and-swap retry delay
values.description: Competing durable compare-and-swap updates can delay pushes when arbitrary hosts concurrently act as primaries.

values.label: Per-repository reference-update latency budget
values.description: Targets bounded write completion latency so a repository sustains a required reference-update rate despite replica distance.

values.label: Minimum two-replica commitment
values.description: An incoming write must be committed to at least two replicas before acceptance.

values.label: Strict-majority write acknowledgment
values.description: Updates are accepted only after a strict majority applies the change and obtains the same result.

values.label: Majority-exclusive write locking
values.description: Each write locks a majority exclusively so conflicting writes cannot both acquire a majority simultaneously.

values.label: Write refusal under insufficient replication
values.description: The system refuses writes when it cannot create the required number of safe copies.

values.label: Availability sacrifice for durability
values.description: Temporary write unavailability results from refusing writes that cannot be safely replicated.

values.label: Quorum-based replica acceptance
values.description: Accept writes only when the configured healthy replica threshold is available.

values.label: Push unavailability without quorum
values.description: Corruption or loss of sufficient healthy copies prevents accepting new pushes.

values.label: Continued write replication during quiescing
values.description: Continue sending writes to a server draining reads so its replica does not fall arbitrarily behind.

values.label: Non-majority write rollback
values.description: Writes not identically applied at a majority are reverted on replicas where they arrived.

values.label: Unhealthy replica exclusion
values.description: Replicas losing a write vote are removed from read and write service until repaired.

values.label: Automatic replica repair
values.description: Unhealthy or lagging replicas are repaired automatically to restore redundancy and service capacity.

values.label: Git reference-update transactions
values.description: Reference changes are coordinated as explicit transactions across replicas.

values.label: Deterministic replica transaction results
values.description: Replica transaction evaluation produces deterministic reference-update results.

values.label: Pre-acquired reference locks
values.description: All local reference locks are acquired before transaction validation and commit.

values.label: Pre-commit reference validation
values.description: Expected old and proposed new reference values are validated before commit.

values.label: Atomic reference-update rollback
values.description: Failed tentative reference transactions are rolled back in full.

values.label: Globally consistent replica reads
values.description: Replica reads remain consistent despite notification loss or topology changes.

values.label: Degraded-correctness healthy-speed behavior
values.description: The replication design preserves correctness during degradation while retaining fast healthy reads.

values.label: Replication consistency complexity cost
values.description: Fully consistent replicas impose substantial implementation complexity.

values.label: WAL-index publication ordering
values.description: Publishing a local reference transaction through an ordered pointer to the durable WAL entry.

values.label: Quorum-free local publication
values.description: Synchronizing reference publication with one local repository instead of a quorum of replicas.

values.label: Eventual replica consistency
values.description: Replicas may temporarily expose divergent repository state after a write.

clusters.name: Repository Service Scaling
clusters.description: Which server-side routing, transfer, failure-detection, maintenance, and platform mechanisms scale repository service workloads?

relations.reading: Repository Service Scaling requires Repository Storage Representation to be decided first
relations.rationale: Synchronized read routing, replica health decisions, and geo-distributed serving depend on knowing replica locations and topology.

values.label: Bookkeeping-update transaction coalescing
values.description: Non-user-critical bookkeeping reference updates are combined to reduce transaction cascades.

values.label: Priority scheduling for user updates
values.description: User-initiated reference updates take priority over maintenance bookkeeping.

values.label: Sync-aware replica selection
values.description: Reads are routed to nearby replicas known to be sufficiently up to date.

values.label: Geographically nearby read replicas
values.description: Fetches and clones are served from replicas close to users to reduce transfer distance.

values.label: Per-application-server failure detectors
values.description: Failure judgments are isolated to application-server and file-server pairs rather than made by one global detector.

values.label: Reference-update processing delay
values.description: Large bookkeeping cascades can keep a repository busy and delay or time out user requests.

values.label: Reduced Git transfer time
values.description: Nearby synchronized replicas reduce Git fetch and clone transfer time.

values.label: Localized failure-detection false positive
values.description: A DNS failure causes one application server to make an incorrect offline determination without affecting other servers.

values.label: No production traffic impact
values.description: The localized detector failure is exposed operationally without affecting production traffic.

values.label: Hidden remote-reference namespace
values.description: Fetched references are stored under a hidden Scalar namespace, supplying commit-graph inputs without changing normal remote-tracking references.

values.label: Separated repository and build-artifact directories
values.description: Keep generated build outputs outside the Git-managed source working directory to reduce working-tree management.

values.label: Centralized missing-object dependency
values.description: Allow clients to depend on a central service to obtain objects absent from the local repository.

values.label: Co-located transfer cache proxy
values.description: Proxy large-repository object requests through cache servers near users and build machines.

values.label: False-positive server removal
values.description: Failure thresholds can temporarily withdraw a healthy server after coincidental consecutive request failures.

values.label: Checksum-guided repository repair scheduling
values.description: Detect damaged repository copies quickly and schedule repair work using continuously tracked validity state.

values.label: Application-traffic failure monitoring
values.description: Use failures observed during real authenticated repository requests, alongside heartbeats, to detect unhealthy servers.

values.label: Custom Git client dependency
values.description: Scaling features depend on a specialized Git client rather than only the standard Git distribution.

values.label: Core Git upstreaming
values.description: Performance capabilities are implemented in and contributed to core Git so specialized-client dependencies can eventually be removed.

values.label: Explicit repository registration
values.description: Users register repositories to activate local configuration and background performance maintenance.

values.label: Automatic Git performance configuration
values.description: Repository registration applies recommended local Git settings automatically.

values.label: Thin Git configuration layer
values.description: The specialized client primarily configures capabilities implemented in standard Git rather than owning parallel implementations.

values.label: Scalar-local performance implementation
values.description: Performance features are implemented only in the specialized Scalar client rather than upstream Git.

values.label: Foreground automatic garbage collection
values.description: Runs repository garbage collection synchronously at command completion or threshold triggers.

values.label: Disabled automatic garbage collection
values.description: Disables automatic garbage collection to avoid synchronous command blocking.

values.label: Horizontal repository-service scalability
values.description: Improves the ability to scale repository-serving capacity across machines and disks.

values.label: Hot-repository availability and performance gaps
values.description: Leaves busy repositories exposed to single-machine availability limits and concentrated performance bottlenecks.

values.label: Foreground maintenance command blocking
values.description: Causes ordinary Git commands to wait while large repository data is rewritten and compressed.

values.label: System-wide maintenance resource exhaustion
values.description: Consumes system CPU and memory during large repository rewrites, potentially halting the machine.

values.label: Repository performance decay
values.description: Gradually degrades Git performance as new objects accumulate without maintenance.

values.label: Read-performance protection during write optimization
values.description: Preserves read responsiveness while optimizing repository writes in read-dominant workloads.

values.label: Packfile transfer burden
values.description: Requires network transfer of Git packfiles even when server-side storage uses another representation.

values.label: Repository hosting reliability objective
values.description: Targets repository availability and dependable service so development and CI continue during failures.

values.label: Repository hosting performance and scale objective
values.description: Targets higher performance and capacity for growing version-control workloads.

values.label: Migration-friendly repository platform
values.description: Provides a low-friction path for moving repositories onto the hosting platform.

values.label: Evolvable repository platform
values.description: Continues adapting repository hosting as version-control workloads and engineering requirements change.

values.label: Agent-driven repository workload growth
values.description: Increases repository, pull-request, and CI demand generated by software agents.

values.label: Development productivity impact of repository downtime
values.description: Makes repository or CI unavailability capable of severely reducing or stopping development productivity.

values.label: Quiesced rolling server reboot
values.description: Servers finish in-progress reads, exclude new reads, and restart sequentially within bounded failure domains.

values.label: Immediate server reboot
values.description: A server restarts without quiescing or completing outstanding reads first.

values.label: Quiesced read admission
values.description: Withdraw a planned-maintenance server from new reads while allowing existing reads to drain.

values.label: Rack-scoped maintenance failure domain
values.description: Maintenance treats each rack as an availability zone and reboots racks sequentially.

values.label: Bounded concurrent reboot count
values.description: Only a limited number of servers reboot concurrently within a maintenance failure domain.

values.label: Temporary reduced-copy state
values.description: A failed or rebooting host temporarily leaves repositories with fewer available copies and reduced failure tolerance.

values.label: Heartbeat load polling
values.description: Heartbeats poll load and signal recovery without serving as the primary failure detector.

values.label: Three-failure offline threshold
values.description: A node is advisory-offline after approximately three consecutive failed operations.

values.label: Operation-level replica failover
values.description: Each failed operation tries the next preferred replica without waiting for centralized detection.

values.label: Preference-ordered replica routing
values.description: Routing returns fresh replicas in preference order for request failover.

values.label: Advisory replica deprioritization
values.description: Repeatedly failing replicas are tried last but retained as available alternatives.

values.label: RPC failover-pattern monitoring
values.description: Patterns of cross-server RPC failover identify unavailable or misbehaving servers.

values.label: Primary-only repository compaction
values.description: Only the primary performs repository compaction to avoid concurrent replica maintenance.

values.label: S3-distributed compacted packs
values.description: Replicas download compacted packs rather than repacking locally.

values.label: Compaction bottleneck
values.description: Git compaction becomes the throughput limit after object-storage latency is reduced.

values.label: Unified repository and WAL compaction
values.description: Compaction updates both the on-disk repository and authoritative log state.

values.label: Replica-side repository repacking
values.description: Each replica independently performs CPU-intensive repository repacking.

values.label: Bandwidth-for-CPU compaction tradeoff
values.description: Replica CPU work is reduced by increasing compacted-pack download bandwidth.

values.label: Replica removal after repeated failures
values.description: Repeatedly failing replicas are removed from routing and replica sets.

values.label: Periodic repository compaction
values.description: Repository compaction runs periodically to bound packfile growth and lookup cost.

values.label: Reference-operation speedups
values.description: Reference operations are optimized to reduce per-replica update time.

values.label: Batched object-storage write processing
values.description: Batching durable object-storage writes rather than imposing independent object-store latency on every push.

values.label: Single object-storage write per push
values.description: Issuing one independently latency-bound object-storage write for each push.

values.label: Transitional Scalar performance layer
values.description: Using Scalar as an interim performance layer while equivalent scalability capabilities move into core Git.

values.label: External repository-placement routing table
values.description: A maintained external table records which hosts contain each repository and supports placement-directed routing.

clusters.name: Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling
clusters.description: Which client-side clone, index, filesystem-monitoring, checkout, and local maintenance mechanisms scale large repositories?

relations.reading: Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling requires Repository Storage Representation to be decided first
relations.rationale: Client clone, index, and maintenance mechanisms depend on the repository representation exposed to clients.

values.label: Partial clone
values.description: Only objects needed for the current checkout are initially transferred to the client.

values.label: Sparse-checkout working tree
values.description: Materialize only selected repository paths, including cone-mode patterns and later selective expansion, to reduce client working-tree scope.

values.label: Compressed Git index
values.description: Index compression reduces client-side repository metadata size.

values.label: Built-in filesystem monitor
values.description: Git's filesystem monitor accelerates status and add operations in repositories with many working-tree files.

values.label: Rails monolith
values.description: The application begins and largely remains a Rails monolith around repository access.

values.label: On-demand object retrieval
values.description: Fetch repository objects dynamically when clients need them instead of transferring the complete object history initially.

values.label: Single-file index management
values.description: Represent and process the complete tracked-path index as one file for core working-directory commands.

values.label: Interrupted clone progress loss
values.description: Immediate server reboot can discard progress from a long-running clone that must restart elsewhere.

values.label: Reduced initial clone footprint
values.description: Filtered object transfer substantially reduces the client download compared with transferring complete repository history.

values.label: Reduced index storage footprint
values.description: An updated index representation lowers storage and I/O burden for repositories with millions of tracked paths.

values.label: Low per-entry index processing cost
values.description: Single-file index processing can retain low average cost per tracked entry despite a very large repository.

values.label: Git untracked cache
values.description: Cache information about untracked paths to reduce repeated working-directory inspection for repositories with many files.

values.label: Default sparse clone initialization
values.description: Client clones initially populate only a minimal directory set, with user-controlled expansion or a full-clone override.

values.label: Populated-file modification detection cost
values.description: Detecting modifications among populated working-directory files imposes additional client-side processing cost.

values.label: Compatibility-limited advanced-feature defaults
values.description: Advanced performance features remain disabled by default when enabling them broadly could reduce compatibility.

values.label: GVFS protocol integration
values.description: Scalar supports the ecosystem-specific GVFS protocol alongside standard Git performance mechanisms.

values.label: GVFS protocol standardization
values.description: The GVFS protocol is made a standard feature of the core Git client.

values.label: Linux support
values.description: The specialized client provides supported Linux operation.

values.label: Git-aware custom filesystem watcher
values.description: Uses a Git-specific watcher that respects repository exclusions instead of a general-purpose filesystem watcher.

values.label: Watchman-based filesystem watching
values.description: Uses the general-purpose Watchman tool to detect working-tree changes.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem working-tree scaling
values.description: Uses a virtualized filesystem to defer populated working-tree costs and accelerate checkout presentation.

values.label: Local Git configuration setup
values.description: Initializes repository-local performance settings as part of enabling the scaling client experience.

values.label: Hourly background fetch
values.description: Remote objects are fetched periodically outside foreground commands while ordinary local and remote-tracking branches remain unchanged.

values.label: Background commit-graph maintenance
values.description: Commit graphs and multi-pack indexes are updated asynchronously to keep large-history operations efficient.

values.label: Incremental reachable-commit graph
values.description: Split incremental commit-graph files include reachable commits while limiting repeated update cost.

values.label: User-suspendable background maintenance
values.description: Automated repository maintenance can be paused or stopped by the user.

values.label: Incremental bounded pack repacking
values.description: Small pack batches are rewritten incrementally to control client repository maintenance cost.

values.label: Multi-pack-index pack migration
values.description: A multi-pack index redirects objects to replacement packs before obsolete packs expire.

values.label: Two-phase repack and expire
values.description: Pack rewriting and obsolete-pack deletion run as separate maintenance operations.

values.label: Background Git object-database maintenance
values.description: Expensive object-database cleanup runs in the background instead of blocking routine commands.

values.label: Ahead/behind calculation suppression
values.description: Interactive status omits expensive ahead/behind comparison.

values.label: Pack-file handle pressure
values.description: Unbounded pack counts create file-handle pressure during Git operations.

values.label: Improved delta-encoding efficiency
values.description: Pack rewriting can improve delta encoding and reduce repository storage.

values.label: Small-pack batch selection
values.description: Each incremental repack selects a bounded set of small packfiles.

values.label: Deferred obsolete-pack deletion
values.description: Old packs are deleted only after index references are safely migrated.

values.label: GVFS deployment without cache infrastructure
values.description: Whether GVFS is deployed without the cache-server infrastructure required for sufficiently large repositories.

values.label: Git-protocol Scalar registration
values.description: Using ordinary Git protocol access with Scalar registration when GVFS infrastructure is unavailable.

values.label: Insufficient scale for GVFS
values.description: Repository and user scale too small to justify GVFS protocol and cache infrastructure.

values.label: Watchman filesystem monitoring
values.description: Using Watchman with Git fsmonitor to detect working-tree changes efficiently.

values.label: Selective modified-path inspection
values.description: Restricting index and cache work to paths reported as changed instead of scanning every populated path.

values.label: Git status latency reduction
values.description: Lowering status latency by avoiding full working-directory inspection in very large repositories.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem working-tree scaling
values.description: Using a virtualized filesystem to scale large-repository working trees by avoiding ordinary Git size assumptions.

values.label: Non-virtualized large-repository support
values.description: Scaling very large repositories with Git and client optimizations without requiring a virtualized filesystem.

values.label: Trace-driven bottleneck identification
values.description: Using tracing and user feedback to identify repository performance bottlenecks for targeted improvements.

values.label: Single-pack full repacking
values.description: Rewriting all repository objects into one consolidated pack-file during maintenance.

values.label: Per-pack index scanning overhead
values.description: Lookup degradation caused by scanning an increasingly large collection of pack indexes.

values.label: Single-pack-equivalent object lookup
values.description: Preserving object lookup performance comparable to a repository consolidated into one pack-file.

iterations.explanation:
Consolidated 200 draft values across 5 dimensions (merge threshold 0.350, borderline band 0.400). Merged 4 near-duplicate values:
  - [Replica Topology and Persistence] "Full checksum recomputation" → "Incremental replica checksum state"
  - [Repository Service Scaling] "Single object-storage write per push" → "Batched object-storage write processing"
  - [Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling] "Watchman filesystem monitoring" → "Watchman-based filesystem watching"
  - [Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling] "Virtualized filesystem working-tree scaling" → "Virtualized filesystem working-tree scaling"
The remaining 192 values were distinct enough to keep as generated.
Evidence linking: 319 of 327 open codes assigned to a value (similarity >= 0.50); 48 of 48 documents now support at least one value.

clusters.name: Repository Storage Representation
clusters.description: Which repository hosting substrate, access form, and Git storage representation is used?

relations.reading: Choices on Repository Storage Representation affect the outcomes of Write Commitment and Consistency
relations.rationale: Replica count and placement determine whether quorum or synchronous durability requirements can be met and influence capacity and latency.

values.label: Centralized repository hosting
values.description: A centralized service provides the primary repository access point despite Git's distributed capabilities.

values.label: Single-machine repository storage
values.description: Application software and repository copies initially coexist on one powerful machine.

values.label: Filesystem-level repository distribution
values.description: Repositories are distributed through the filesystem layer to scale application instances without changing Rails or Git internals.

values.label: NFS-based centralized repository storage
values.description: NFS is considered for centralized storage but rejected because Git's local-filesystem assumptions do not work safely or efficiently over it.

values.label: DHT-backed Git object storage
values.description: Stores individual Git objects in a distributed hash table instead of repository packfiles.

values.label: Object-level repository distribution
values.description: Distributes individual content-addressed objects across storage nodes rather than preserving repository-level packfile organization.

values.label: JGit repository-storage abstraction
values.description: Uses replaceable JGit storage interfaces to change repository storage while retaining Git operations.

values.label: Packfile-based repository storage
values.description: Stores repository code and metadata in compressed Git packfiles.

values.label: Dedicated fileserver repository hosting
values.description: Keeps repositories on dedicated fileservers and exposes repository operations through remote procedure calls.

values.label: Whole-file local repository caching
values.description: Caches a complete repository file locally to accelerate random access to repository data.

values.label: Delta-compressed packfile storage
values.description: Stores most packfile objects as deltas to reduce storage size at the cost of additional read hops.

values.label: Packfile-based Git networking
values.description: Uses Git packfiles as the client-server transfer representation regardless of internal server storage.

values.label: Packfile size-minimizing layout
values.description: Places Git objects in packfiles using a compact size-minimization heuristic rather than preserving repository-DAG locality.

values.label: Git-level distribution
values.description: Repository distribution modifies or distributes Git itself rather than replicating repository data above it.

values.label: Repository-data transformation
values.description: Repository contents are transformed into a separate client-facing storage format.

values.label: Application layer over unmodified Git
values.description: Hosting features are built above standard Git repositories without maintaining a Git fork.

values.label: Plain Git repositories on local NVMe
values.description: Native repositories are stored on local NVMe for random-read performance and client compatibility.

values.label: Networked-filesystem repository access
values.description: The attempted networked-filesystem approach produces poor performance and buggy behavior because of mismatched filesystem assumptions.

clusters.name: Replica Topology and Persistence
clusters.description: Which replica placement and durable state model maintains repository copies across failures?

relations.reading: Choices on Replica Topology and Persistence affect the outcomes of Write Commitment and Consistency
relations.rationale: S3-backed authoritative state, freshness validation, and elastic replica topology change consistency and write-commitment behavior.

values.label: Cross-rack replica placement
values.description: Replicas are distributed across racks to survive rack-level failures as well as individual node failures.

values.label: Three-replica repository topology
values.description: Each repository receives at least three copies to provide redundancy and capacity for continued operation after one machine failure.

values.label: Single-extra-copy topology
values.description: Keeping only one additional copy is considered sufficient for a single-node failure but rejected because concurrent writes still require consistent serialization.

values.label: Write-ahead-log repository persistence
values.description: Authoritative repository state and provenance persist in a durable write-ahead log rather than fixed host placement.

values.label: Relational reference database persistence
values.description: Store repository references in an external relational database alongside blob or packfile storage.

values.label: Incremental replica checksum state
values.description: Maintain logical repository-state checksums incrementally rather than recomputing them from all references.

values.label: Stateless repository placement
values.description: Repository placement is resolved from current healthy hosts without maintaining an external per-repository routing table.

values.label: Git application-level replication
values.description: Repository replication operates on Git-aware updates rather than filesystem blocks.

values.label: Proxy-mediated repository replication
values.description: A proxy transparently forwards each Git push to multiple repository replicas.

values.label: Low-latency replica placement
values.description: Replicas are placed near enough to coordinate updates within acceptable inter-replica communication latency.

values.label: Disk repository warm cache
values.description: Local disk repositories serve as reconstructible caches rather than fixed authoritative placement.

values.label: On-demand repository materialization
values.description: A host reconstructs an absent repository locally from durable log state when requests require it.

values.label: Rendezvous-hash placement hints
values.description: Repository identifiers rank expected healthy hosts without requiring authoritative placement state.

values.label: N-to-N replica reconstruction
values.description: Replacement replicas are created across the cluster from any surviving repository copies after failures.

values.label: ETag-validated replica freshness
values.description: Conditional object-store metadata validation confirms replica freshness before serving reads.

values.label: Read-time replica catch-up
values.description: Replicas apply newer durable log state before serving a read.

values.label: Elastic per-repository replica allocation
values.description: Replica count expands or contracts according to repository read demand and durable-source availability.

values.label: WAL-propagated compaction state
values.description: Compaction state is propagated through the authoritative log to keep replicas aligned.

values.label: Optimistic UDP catch-up gossip
values.description: Replicas exchange catch-up metadata through lossy gossip while durable reads independently validate freshness.

values.label: Compacted-data replica distribution
values.description: Replicas receive compacted repository data rather than maintaining unrelated storage states.

values.label: Arbitrary replica-based read scaling
values.description: Read replicas can be deployed in arbitrary numbers to scale read-only operations.

values.label: File-server content replication
values.description: Replicating repository and gist content stored on file servers across the application’s server fleet.

values.label: Repository repair and rebalancing
values.description: Repairing and redistributing repository copies as servers and networks fail or topology changes.

values.label: Disk-backed repository source of truth
values.description: Repository data on local disks is treated as authoritative state rather than merely a reconstructible cache.

values.label: Filesystem block-level replication
values.description: Repository replicas are synchronized through filesystem block replication below Git's application semantics.

values.label: Co-located filesystem replica placement
values.description: Keeps filesystem replicas adjacent to control replication latency, rather than separating them across racks or sites.

values.label: S3 Express object-storage substrate
values.description: A low-latency object-storage tier is selected for high-throughput WAL persistence.

values.label: Idle-replica overhead
values.description: Maintaining three mostly idle replicas per small or throwaway repository creates substantial overhead as repository counts proliferate.

values.label: Monorepo traffic capacity shortfall
values.description: Three replicas become insufficient for traffic from massive enterprise monorepos, especially continuous-integration traffic.

values.label: Pet-repository operational burden
values.description: Continuously tracking repository locations, validity, failures, and repairs creates substantial operational cost at scale.

values.label: Durable highly available content access
values.description: Maintaining durable, highly available repository and gist access through copies distributed across failures.

clusters.name: Write Commitment and Consistency
clusters.description: Which consistency, acknowledgment, locking, and refusal policy governs accepting repository writes?

relations.reading: Choices on Write Commitment and Consistency affect the outcomes of Repository Service Scaling
relations.rationale: Synchronous commitment, quorum locking, and refusal during insufficient replication can increase write latency or temporary request unavailability.

values.label: Three-phase commit consensus
values.description: Three-phase commit coordinates repository writes in a way that maps to the Git transaction model.

values.label: Consistency and partition tolerance priority
values.description: The system prioritizes consistency and partition tolerance over availability when those qualities conflict.

values.label: Synchronous write commitment
values.description: A write is accepted only after synchronous commitment establishes the durability promise.

values.label: Permanent data-loss resistance
values.description: Accepted pushes, merges, edits, and repository creations must not be corrupted or reverted.

values.label: Non-voting geo-replicated hosts
values.description: Geographically replicated hosts do not vote, allowing primary pushes to continue when a replicated host is unreachable.

values.label: WAL durability before push acknowledgement
values.description: Require durable operation-log persistence before reporting a successful push to the client.

values.label: Linearized repository operations
values.description: Process pushes and fundamental repository operations in one consistent order.

values.label: Operation-history replica rewind
values.description: Use recorded repository operations to rewind and fast-forward replicas without synchronizing through an external object or reference database.

values.label: Replica-based distributed locking
values.description: Replica coordination supplies distributed locks that order repository database updates.

values.label: Per-write ordering election
values.description: Each write directly elects its winning order and outcome instead of relying on a permanently elected primary.

values.label: Single-primary replication model
values.description: One elected primary copy determines authoritative write-arrival order for all replicas.

values.label: Overlapped replica coordination work
values.description: Useful locking, checksum, and database work proceeds while replica network waits are outstanding.

values.label: Consensus-free arbitrary repository primaries
values.description: Any healthy server may accept a push without election because durable compare-and-swap synchronization makes concurrent updates safe.

values.label: Rendezvous-ranked primary preference
values.description: The highest-ranked healthy host is preferred to reduce compare-and-swap retries while other hosts remain valid.

values.label: Minimum two-replica commitment
values.description: An incoming write must be committed to at least two replicas before acceptance.

values.label: Strict-majority write acknowledgment
values.description: Updates are accepted only after a strict majority applies the change and obtains the same result.

values.label: Majority-exclusive write locking
values.description: Each write locks a majority exclusively so conflicting writes cannot both acquire a majority simultaneously.

values.label: Write refusal under insufficient replication
values.description: The system refuses writes when it cannot create the required number of safe copies.

values.label: Quorum-based replica acceptance
values.description: Accept writes only when the configured healthy replica threshold is available.

values.label: Continued write replication during quiescing
values.description: Continue sending writes to a server draining reads so its replica does not fall arbitrarily behind.

values.label: Non-majority write rollback
values.description: Writes not identically applied at a majority are reverted on replicas where they arrived.

values.label: Unhealthy replica exclusion
values.description: Replicas losing a write vote are removed from read and write service until repaired.

values.label: Automatic replica repair
values.description: Unhealthy or lagging replicas are repaired automatically to restore redundancy and service capacity.

values.label: Git reference-update transactions
values.description: Reference changes are coordinated as explicit transactions across replicas.

values.label: Deterministic replica transaction results
values.description: Replica transaction evaluation produces deterministic reference-update results.

values.label: Pre-acquired reference locks
values.description: All local reference locks are acquired before transaction validation and commit.

values.label: Pre-commit reference validation
values.description: Expected old and proposed new reference values are validated before commit.

values.label: Atomic reference-update rollback
values.description: Failed tentative reference transactions are rolled back in full.

values.label: WAL-index publication ordering
values.description: Publishing a local reference transaction through an ordered pointer to the durable WAL entry.

values.label: Quorum-free local publication
values.description: Synchronizing reference publication with one local repository instead of a quorum of replicas.

values.label: Eventual replica consistency
values.description: Replicas may temporarily expose divergent repository state after a write.

values.label: Consensus tail-latency growth
values.description: Adding replicas increases the influence of the slowest participant on three-phase-commit latency.

values.label: Replica-count push-throughput degradation
values.description: Push throughput worsens as more replicas participate in three-phase commit.

values.label: Replica coordination round-trip cost
values.description: Distributed replica coordination requires multiple network round trips, adding latency to repository operations.

values.label: Compare-and-swap retry delay
values.description: Competing durable compare-and-swap updates can delay pushes when arbitrary hosts concurrently act as primaries.

values.label: Per-repository reference-update latency budget
values.description: Targets bounded write completion latency so a repository sustains a required reference-update rate despite replica distance.

values.label: Availability sacrifice for durability
values.description: Temporary write unavailability results from refusing writes that cannot be safely replicated.

values.label: Push unavailability without quorum
values.description: Corruption or loss of sufficient healthy copies prevents accepting new pushes.

values.label: Globally consistent replica reads
values.description: Replica reads remain consistent despite notification loss or topology changes.

values.label: Degraded-correctness healthy-speed behavior
values.description: The replication design preserves correctness during degradation while retaining fast healthy reads.

values.label: Replication consistency complexity cost
values.description: Fully consistent replicas impose substantial implementation complexity.

clusters.name: Repository Service Scaling
clusters.description: Which server-side routing, transfer, failure-detection, maintenance, and platform mechanisms scale repository service workloads?

relations.reading: Repository Service Scaling requires Repository Storage Representation to be decided first
relations.rationale: Synchronized read routing, replica health decisions, and geo-distributed serving depend on knowing replica locations and topology.

values.label: Bookkeeping-update transaction coalescing
values.description: Non-user-critical bookkeeping reference updates are combined to reduce transaction cascades.

values.label: Priority scheduling for user updates
values.description: User-initiated reference updates take priority over maintenance bookkeeping.

values.label: Sync-aware replica selection
values.description: Reads are routed to nearby replicas known to be sufficiently up to date.

values.label: Geographically nearby read replicas
values.description: Fetches and clones are served from replicas close to users to reduce transfer distance.

values.label: Per-application-server failure detectors
values.description: Failure judgments are isolated to application-server and file-server pairs rather than made by one global detector.

values.label: Hidden remote-reference namespace
values.description: Fetched references are stored under a hidden Scalar namespace, supplying commit-graph inputs without changing normal remote-tracking references.

values.label: Separated repository and build-artifact directories
values.description: Keep generated build outputs outside the Git-managed source working directory to reduce working-tree management.

values.label: Centralized missing-object dependency
values.description: Allow clients to depend on a central service to obtain objects absent from the local repository.

values.label: Co-located transfer cache proxy
values.description: Proxy large-repository object requests through cache servers near users and build machines.

values.label: Checksum-guided repository repair scheduling
values.description: Detect damaged repository copies quickly and schedule repair work using continuously tracked validity state.

values.label: Application-traffic failure monitoring
values.description: Use failures observed during real authenticated repository requests, alongside heartbeats, to detect unhealthy servers.

values.label: Custom Git client dependency
values.description: Scaling features depend on a specialized Git client rather than only the standard Git distribution.

values.label: Core Git upstreaming
values.description: Performance capabilities are implemented in and contributed to core Git so specialized-client dependencies can eventually be removed.

values.label: Explicit repository registration
values.description: Users register repositories to activate local configuration and background performance maintenance.

values.label: Automatic Git performance configuration
values.description: Repository registration applies recommended local Git settings automatically.

values.label: Thin Git configuration layer
values.description: The specialized client primarily configures capabilities implemented in standard Git rather than owning parallel implementations.

values.label: Scalar-local performance implementation
values.description: Performance features are implemented only in the specialized Scalar client rather than upstream Git.

values.label: Foreground automatic garbage collection
values.description: Runs repository garbage collection synchronously at command completion or threshold triggers.

values.label: Disabled automatic garbage collection
values.description: Disables automatic garbage collection to avoid synchronous command blocking.

values.label: Repository hosting reliability objective
values.description: Targets repository availability and dependable service so development and CI continue during failures.

values.label: Repository hosting performance and scale objective
values.description: Targets higher performance and capacity for growing version-control workloads.

values.label: Migration-friendly repository platform
values.description: Provides a low-friction path for moving repositories onto the hosting platform.

values.label: Evolvable repository platform
values.description: Continues adapting repository hosting as version-control workloads and engineering requirements change.

values.label: Quiesced rolling server reboot
values.description: Servers finish in-progress reads, exclude new reads, and restart sequentially within bounded failure domains.

values.label: Immediate server reboot
values.description: A server restarts without quiescing or completing outstanding reads first.

values.label: Quiesced read admission
values.description: Withdraw a planned-maintenance server from new reads while allowing existing reads to drain.

values.label: Rack-scoped maintenance failure domain
values.description: Maintenance treats each rack as an availability zone and reboots racks sequentially.

values.label: Bounded concurrent reboot count
values.description: Only a limited number of servers reboot concurrently within a maintenance failure domain.

values.label: Heartbeat load polling
values.description: Heartbeats poll load and signal recovery without serving as the primary failure detector.

values.label: Three-failure offline threshold
values.description: A node is advisory-offline after approximately three consecutive failed operations.

values.label: Operation-level replica failover
values.description: Each failed operation tries the next preferred replica without waiting for centralized detection.

values.label: Preference-ordered replica routing
values.description: Routing returns fresh replicas in preference order for request failover.

values.label: Advisory replica deprioritization
values.description: Repeatedly failing replicas are tried last but retained as available alternatives.

values.label: RPC failover-pattern monitoring
values.description: Patterns of cross-server RPC failover identify unavailable or misbehaving servers.

values.label: Primary-only repository compaction
values.description: Only the primary performs repository compaction to avoid concurrent replica maintenance.

values.label: S3-distributed compacted packs
values.description: Replicas download compacted packs rather than repacking locally.

values.label: Unified repository and WAL compaction
values.description: Compaction updates both the on-disk repository and authoritative log state.

values.label: Replica-side repository repacking
values.description: Each replica independently performs CPU-intensive repository repacking.

values.label: Replica removal after repeated failures
values.description: Repeatedly failing replicas are removed from routing and replica sets.

values.label: Periodic repository compaction
values.description: Repository compaction runs periodically to bound packfile growth and lookup cost.

values.label: Reference-operation speedups
values.description: Reference operations are optimized to reduce per-replica update time.

values.label: Batched object-storage write processing
values.description: Batching durable object-storage writes rather than imposing independent object-store latency on every push.

values.label: Transitional Scalar performance layer
values.description: Using Scalar as an interim performance layer while equivalent scalability capabilities move into core Git.

values.label: External repository-placement routing table
values.description: A maintained external table records which hosts contain each repository and supports placement-directed routing.

values.label: Reference-update processing delay
values.description: Large bookkeeping cascades can keep a repository busy and delay or time out user requests.

values.label: Reduced Git transfer time
values.description: Nearby synchronized replicas reduce Git fetch and clone transfer time.

values.label: Localized failure-detection false positive
values.description: A DNS failure causes one application server to make an incorrect offline determination without affecting other servers.

values.label: No production traffic impact
values.description: The localized detector failure is exposed operationally without affecting production traffic.

values.label: False-positive server removal
values.description: Failure thresholds can temporarily withdraw a healthy server after coincidental consecutive request failures.

values.label: Horizontal repository-service scalability
values.description: Improves the ability to scale repository-serving capacity across machines and disks.

values.label: Hot-repository availability and performance gaps
values.description: Leaves busy repositories exposed to single-machine availability limits and concentrated performance bottlenecks.

values.label: Foreground maintenance command blocking
values.description: Causes ordinary Git commands to wait while large repository data is rewritten and compressed.

values.label: System-wide maintenance resource exhaustion
values.description: Consumes system CPU and memory during large repository rewrites, potentially halting the machine.

values.label: Repository performance decay
values.description: Gradually degrades Git performance as new objects accumulate without maintenance.

values.label: Read-performance protection during write optimization
values.description: Preserves read responsiveness while optimizing repository writes in read-dominant workloads.

values.label: Packfile transfer burden
values.description: Requires network transfer of Git packfiles even when server-side storage uses another representation.

values.label: Agent-driven repository workload growth
values.description: Increases repository, pull-request, and CI demand generated by software agents.

values.label: Development productivity impact of repository downtime
values.description: Makes repository or CI unavailability capable of severely reducing or stopping development productivity.

values.label: Temporary reduced-copy state
values.description: A failed or rebooting host temporarily leaves repositories with fewer available copies and reduced failure tolerance.

values.label: Compaction bottleneck
values.description: Git compaction becomes the throughput limit after object-storage latency is reduced.

values.label: Bandwidth-for-CPU compaction tradeoff
values.description: Replica CPU work is reduced by increasing compacted-pack download bandwidth.

clusters.name: Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling
clusters.description: Which client-side clone, index, filesystem-monitoring, checkout, and local maintenance mechanisms scale large repositories?

relations.reading: Client Repository and Working-Tree Scaling requires Repository Storage Representation to be decided first
relations.rationale: Client clone, index, and maintenance mechanisms depend on the repository representation exposed to clients.

values.label: Partial clone
values.description: Only objects needed for the current checkout are initially transferred to the client.

values.label: Sparse-checkout working tree
values.description: Materialize only selected repository paths, including cone-mode patterns and later selective expansion, to reduce client working-tree scope.

values.label: Compressed Git index
values.description: Index compression reduces client-side repository metadata size.

values.label: Built-in filesystem monitor
values.description: Git's filesystem monitor accelerates status and add operations in repositories with many working-tree files.

values.label: Rails monolith
values.description: The application begins and largely remains a Rails monolith around repository access.

values.label: On-demand object retrieval
values.description: Fetch repository objects dynamically when clients need them instead of transferring the complete object history initially.

values.label: Single-file index management
values.description: Represent and process the complete tracked-path index as one file for core working-directory commands.

values.label: Git untracked cache
values.description: Cache information about untracked paths to reduce repeated working-directory inspection for repositories with many files.

values.label: Default sparse clone initialization
values.description: Client clones initially populate only a minimal directory set, with user-controlled expansion or a full-clone override.

values.label: GVFS protocol integration
values.description: Scalar supports the ecosystem-specific GVFS protocol alongside standard Git performance mechanisms.

values.label: GVFS protocol standardization
values.description: The GVFS protocol is made a standard feature of the core Git client.

values.label: Git-aware custom filesystem watcher
values.description: Uses a Git-specific watcher that respects repository exclusions instead of a general-purpose filesystem watcher.

values.label: Watchman-based filesystem watching
values.description: Uses the general-purpose Watchman tool to detect working-tree changes.

values.label: Virtualized filesystem working-tree scaling
values.description: Uses a virtualized filesystem to defer populated working-tree costs and accelerate checkout presentation.

values.label: Local Git configuration setup
values.description: Initializes repository-local performance settings as part of enabling the scaling client experience.

values.label: Hourly background fetch
values.description: Remote objects are fetched periodically outside foreground commands while ordinary local and remote-tracking branches remain unchanged.

values.label: Background commit-graph maintenance
values.description: Commit graphs and multi-pack indexes are updated asynchronously to keep large-history operations efficient.

values.label: Incremental reachable-commit graph
values.description: Split incremental commit-graph files include reachable commits while limiting repeated update cost.

values.label: User-suspendable background maintenance
values.description: Automated repository maintenance can be paused or stopped by the user.

values.label: Incremental bounded pack repacking
values.description: Small pack batches are rewritten incrementally to control client repository maintenance cost.

values.label: Multi-pack-index pack migration
values.description: A multi-pack index redirects objects to replacement packs before obsolete packs expire.

values.label: Two-phase repack and expire
values.description: Pack rewriting and obsolete-pack deletion run as separate maintenance operations.

values.label: Background Git object-database maintenance
values.description: Expensive object-database cleanup runs in the background instead of blocking routine commands.

values.label: Ahead/behind calculation suppression
values.description: Interactive status omits expensive ahead/behind comparison.

values.label: Small-pack batch selection
values.description: Each incremental repack selects a bounded set of small packfiles.

values.label: Deferred obsolete-pack deletion
values.description: Old packs are deleted only after index references are safely migrated.

values.label: GVFS deployment without cache infrastructure
values.description: Whether GVFS is deployed without the cache-server infrastructure required for sufficiently large repositories.

values.label: Git-protocol Scalar registration
values.description: Using ordinary Git protocol access with Scalar registration when GVFS infrastructure is unavailable.

values.label: Non-virtualized large-repository support
values.description: Scaling very large repositories with Git and client optimizations without requiring a virtualized filesystem.

values.label: Trace-driven bottleneck identification
values.description: Using tracing and user feedback to identify repository performance bottlenecks for targeted improvements.

values.label: Single-pack full repacking
values.description: Rewriting all repository objects into one consolidated pack-file during maintenance.

values.label: Interrupted clone progress loss
values.description: Immediate server reboot can discard progress from a long-running clone that must restart elsewhere.

values.label: Reduced initial clone footprint
values.description: Filtered object transfer substantially reduces the client download compared with transferring complete repository history.

values.label: Reduced index storage footprint
values.description: An updated index representation lowers storage and I/O burden for repositories with millions of tracked paths.

values.label: Low per-entry index processing cost
values.description: Single-file index processing can retain low average cost per tracked entry despite a very large repository.

values.label: Populated-file modification detection cost
values.description: Detecting modifications among populated working-directory files imposes additional client-side processing cost.

values.label: Compatibility-limited advanced-feature defaults
values.description: Advanced performance features remain disabled by default when enabling them broadly could reduce compatibility.

values.label: Linux support
values.description: The specialized client provides supported Linux operation.

values.label: Pack-file handle pressure
values.description: Unbounded pack counts create file-handle pressure during Git operations.

values.label: Improved delta-encoding efficiency
values.description: Pack rewriting can improve delta encoding and reduce repository storage.

values.label: Insufficient scale for GVFS
values.description: Repository and user scale too small to justify GVFS protocol and cache infrastructure.

values.label: Selective modified-path inspection
values.description: Restricting index and cache work to paths reported as changed instead of scanning every populated path.

values.label: Git status latency reduction
values.description: Lowering status latency by avoiding full working-directory inspection in very large repositories.

values.label: Per-pack index scanning overhead
values.description: Lookup degradation caused by scanning an increasingly large collection of pack indexes.

values.label: Single-pack-equivalent object lookup
values.description: Preserving object lookup performance comparable to a repository consolidated into one pack-file.
